label: Church of God (Cleveland, TN)
framing: Frame for a Church of God (Cleveland, TN) audience using the Declaration of Faith: Trinitarian classical Pentecostal with Holiness roots—sanctification subsequent to the new birth, baptism in the Holy Ghost subsequent to a clean heart, tongues as initial evidence, and divine healing. Avoid inventing experiences.
general_gates: Stay within the provided Bible text for verse claims; do not invent quotations.
Do not invent primary-source citations beyond the digests and Declaration of Faith pointers in this pack.
When citing Church of God doctrine, use only the Declaration of Faith items listed in the Cited references block.
Keep Trinitarian framing; water baptism is in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.
Do not invent personal prophetic words, healings, or Spirit-baptism experiences as facts about the user.
For sensitive life topics, encourage prayer and trusted pastoral or professional help; AI is not a substitute for counseling.

citation_map.note: Verbal inspiration of the Bible. Cite Declaration item 1.
Repentance, justification/regeneration by faith, sanctification subsequent to the new birth, and holiness as God’s standard. Cite items 4–7.
Baptism with the Holy Ghost subsequent to a clean heart; speaking with other tongues as initial evidence. Cite items 8–9.
Water baptism by immersion in the Triune name; Lord’s Supper and washing of the saints’ feet. Cite items 10 and 12.
Divine healing is provided for all in the atonement. Cite item 11.
Premillennial second coming; bodily resurrection and eternal destinies. Cite items 13–14.

primary_sources.title: Church of God — Declaration of Faith (digest)
primary_sources.excerpt: Fourteen concise statements: inspired Bible; Trinity; Christ; repentance and new birth; sanctification subsequent to the new birth; holiness; Spirit baptism subsequent to a clean heart with tongues as initial evidence; Triune water baptism; divine healing; Lord’s Supper and footwashing; premillennial return; resurrection and judgment.

primary_sources.title: Church of God — sanctification (digest)
primary_sources.excerpt: Sanctification is taught as subsequent to the new birth through faith in Christ’s blood, the Word, and the Holy Ghost. Holiness is God’s standard. Spirit baptism follows a clean heart.

stances.summary: Per the Declaration, sanctification is subsequent to the new birth; holiness is God’s standard for His people.
forbid: collapse sanctification into conversion only when explaining COG doctrine

stances.summary: Sanctification is a distinct work subsequent to the new birth in Church of God framing.
conditions: faith in Christ’s blood, Word, and Spirit

stances.summary: Spirit baptism is subsequent to a clean heart; tongues is the initial evidence.
